column1: # Shape answer key — objectively checkable items a good framing must contain.
# correctness = (rows marked caught) / (total rows). Equal weight.

column2: Separates the two conflated needs: (a) what setup changed, (b) where the project is in the lifecycle.
States success criteria in observable terms (e.g. operator can answer "what changed / where am I" without re-running anything).
Names the zero-dependency / POSIX-bash constraint (ADR-0003) so proposed issues cannot assume a new runtime.
Surveys existing assets rather than proposing greenfield: cites at least `spark brief`, `spark resume`, and `.spark/state.json`.
Decomposes into at least two independently shippable issues, each with explicit acceptance criteria.
Assigns the issues to a milestone (or an explicit backlog decision) and preserves the human as approver — no scope is auto-accepted.
Does not prematurely commit to one implementation; the problem statement stays solution-neutral.
